actions.action: Check for root-bound signs: fast-draining or fast-drying soil, top-heaviness, circling roots, slowed growth
Buy a pot one size larger (about 30–33 cm)
Buy or mix chunky well-draining soil (potting soil with about 30% perlite or bark, plus orchid bark)
Repot in spring or early summer at the same depth
Gently loosen outer roots and trim dead or mushy roots
Free or cut roots stuck through the drainage holes
Optionally divide the multiple plants while repotting

reason: The answer identifies the plant as root-bound and recommends repotting one size up, matching the confirmed fix; calling it non-urgent is a mild delay but not harmful.
